title: Redwood x AuroraCloud - Marketplace & Reference Arch Sync
summary: Sync between Redwood AE/SE and AuroraCloud partner team to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for joint solution, billing/metering expectations, and go-live timeline. Technical deep-dive on VPC/private deployment options, SSO/SAML, packaging (container vs AMI), and test plan. Agreed next steps and owners for artifacts and staging test window.
next_steps: Maya to share reference architecture diagram and sample deployment manifest by 2026-10-09
Ethan to send marketplace checklist and listing template by 2026-10-08
AuroraCloud to provision staging account for integration tests by 2026-10-14

Ethan Cole (AE): share marketplace checklist and pricing template - due 2026-10-08
Anika Sharma (Cloud Engineer): create staging environment and provide credentials (read-only) - due 2026-10-14

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-07 14:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Ethan Cole, Maya Liu (Redwood); Carlos Mendes, Anika Sharma, Priya Rao (AuroraCloud)

Summary: quick sync to align on marketplace listing + reference architecture and integration steps. Some audio drop-outs early, transcription imperfect in a few places.

00:00:05 - Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on the account. Maya from our SE team will run the tech bits.
00:00:15 - Carlos: Hi, thanks, yeah. We want to make sure the marketplace listing process is smooth and the reference arch matches our ops constraints.
00:00:30 - Maya: Great, I'll go through our recommended reference architecture and then we can map to the AuroraCloud marketplace requirements. Quick note, forgive any auto-transcript typos — sometimes it writes K-V cache as kitty cache, so just assume some words are off.
00:01:05 - Ethan: Quick agenda: 1) listing metadata and packaging (container vs AMI), 2) networking & deployment (VPC peering, Private), 3) security/compliance (SSO, SAML, KMS), 4) metering/billing, 5) timelines.
00:02:20 - Carlos: For AuroraCloud, partners need to support both container images and a marketplace VM image. Is Redwood flexible on packaging?
00:02:35 - Maya: Yes, we support containerized deployment (recommended for Dedicated/Private) and AMI-style images for on-prem or certain marketplace flows. The runtime is GPU-optimized so for containers you'll want base images with CUDA drivers if you plan to use dedicated GPU nodes. For hosted listing, the API integration is lighter — we provide an integration manifest and OAuth flow.
00:03:50 - Anika: For our side, networking is critical. We require VPC peering or PrivateLink, and ability to use our KMS with customer-managed keys. How does Redwood handle KMS/HSM flows?
00:04:05 - Maya: We integrate with KMS providers; for Private deployments we can wire to customer KMS or HSM. There are two patterns: 1) Redwood-managed control plane + customer KMS via cross-account IAM, 2) fully customer-hosted control plane in VPC (air-gapped) where keys never leave your environment. We'll attach the diagram in the reference arch.
00:05:30 - Carlos: That second pattern sounds closer to what our security team prefers for some enterprise customers. Latency wise, any trade-offs?
00:05:45 - Maya: Slight added latency for private-hosted control plane if it's not colocated, but it's typically within SLOs if you provision appropriate instances. We'll include quantization and batching guidance to keep token latency low.
00:06:40 - Ethan: On marketplace listing metadata, AuroraCloud needs usage-based metering fields and a pricing schema. Do you want per-token pricing, per-hour reserved, or hybrid?
00:06:55 - Priya: AuroraCloud generally supports both metering by API call/consumption and reserved subscriptions. Partners typically provide both: per-token for hosted and reserved capacity options for enterprise buyers.
00:07:30 - Maya: Redwood can emit usage logs to your billing system — we can do metering hooks, usage reports, or S3 ingestion. Need to confirm the schema. We'll share an example usage feed.
00:08:10 - Anika: Also need to surface region availability metadata in the listing — e.g., which regions support GPU-backed instances.
00:08:25 - Maya: We'll include a region matrix in the reference doc.
00:09:00 - Ethan: Security checklist: SOC2 attestation, SSO (SAML/OIDC) support, RBAC in console, audit logs, data retention options. Which of these do you want called out in the marketplace tile?
00:09:15 - Priya: All of them ideally; at minimum SOC2, SSO, and encryption with KMS. We'll need the compliance artifacts attached for the listing.
00:09:45 - Maya: We can share SOC2 report (redacted), an SSO integration guide, and how audit logs are surfaced. There's sometimes transcription garbage where it says "RRBC" instead of RBAC but we'll make the doc clear.
00:10:30 - Carlos: Technical deep dive: can we talk about model packaging and kernel selection? On our end we want to ensure models can be pinned and rolled back.
00:10:45 - Maya: Absolutely. Redwood's serving runtime supports pinning model versions and rollouts (canary/A-B). For on-prem deployments we provide a model artifact bundle and a runtime manifest — includes quantization profile, kernel hints, and sequence length defaults. We also have fallback model variants if capacity constrained.
00:11:40 - Anika: For deployment, do you expect us to expose CUDA drivers ourselves or do you want Redwood to provide driver-managed images?
00:11:55 - Maya: We provide base images that include drivers for common GPU families. If you have custom hardware, you can provide a custom base image. We'll document recommended driver and CUDA versions.
00:12:30 - Ethan: Questions from our side about testing: what's your acceptance criteria for marketplace QA?
00:12:45 - Priya: We'll need a staging test that verifies provisioning, SSO login, an inference smoke test (latency and correctness), and billing event emission. The legal/ops side will also validate the listing metadata and terms.
00:13:20 - Maya: For performance smoke tests we usually run a 5k token throughput test and a 95th percentile latency check at several batch sizes, plus a small regression set to check quality. We'll share our benchmark harness.
00:14:40 - Ethan: Do you have any particular legal/pre-reqs — e.g., data residency or custom clauses?
00:14:55 - Carlos: Some enterprise customers will require explicit data residency in EU or APAC — the listing needs to indicate available regions and any restrictions.
00:15:20 - Maya: Noted. We'll add region availability and recommended deployment patterns per region.
00:16:00 - [00:16:22] - Anika: On the integration manifest, is there a standard schema? We want to auto-ingest it into our marketplace onboarding pipeline.
00:16:35 - Ethan: We have a marketplace template we fill; I'll attach the template after the meeting. It includes fields for endpoint, auth type, resource types (GPU families), pricing tiers, and the manifest URL.
00:17:10 - Priya: Timeline question — what's realistic for staging -> listing?
00:17:25 - Maya: If we get staging access and the artifacts this week, typically 2-3 weeks for integration and QA, so a mid-late October listing looks feasible. But that depends on legal review and your marketplace backlog.
00:17:55 - Carlos: That aligns with our internal timeline. We aim for public listing by November if possible.
00:18:20 - Maya: A couple of technical flags: 1) prefix/KV cache wins for customer workloads — please share typical sequence lengths, 2) batching settings per endpoint, 3) default quantization profile for balanced quality/cost.
00:18:45 - Anika: We'll export some sample workloads. Sequence lengths average 512 tokens with peaks to 2048 for some tasks.
00:19:05 - Maya: Good — we'll recommend a profile accordingly.
00:20:30 - [00:20:45] - Ethan: Let's cover SSO flow quickly. Do you prefer SAML or OIDC?
00:20:55 - Priya: AuroraCloud supports both; for marketplace provisioning we prefer OIDC for service accounts and SAML for end-user SSO.
00:21:10 - Maya: We can provide both. For provisioning we use a client credential flow with scoped tokens; for user SSO we support SAML assertions and map attributes to RBAC roles.
00:21:45 - Anika: About audit logs — can logs be shipped to our SIEM (S3/HTTP/CloudWatch)?
00:21:55 - Maya: Yes, we support S3 delivery, a push webhook, or Cloud-native integrations. We'll include sample log schema.
00:22:30 - [00:22:45] - Ethan: Onto billing: what fields do you need in metering events?
00:22:55 - Priya: Timestamp, customer_id, resource_id, tokens_consumed, model_id, region, and a usage_event_id for idempotency.
00:23:20 - Maya: We'll adapt our usage feed to include those fields.
00:23:50 - Carlos: Any blockers we foresee?

00:24:05 - Maya: The main things are: staging provisioning creds, KMS/key ownership decision, and whether Aurora wants the control plane to be customer-hosted or Redwood-managed for the initial listing.
00:24:25 - Anika: Security prefers customer-hosted control plane for enterprise tier, but for the initial marketplace MVP we could do Redwood-managed with cross-account KMS. That would speed up go-live.
00:24:45 - Ethan: Trade-off is speed vs compliance. We recommend Redwood-managed for MVP then transition to customer-hosted for enterprise customers.
00:25:10 - Priya: That approach works for us. We'll note it in the PM plan.
00:25:35 - [00:25:50] - Maya: We'll attach a sample deployment manifest and a reference arch diagram showing 3 patterns: 1) Hosted API listing, 2) Dedicated/reserved capacity with VPC peering, 3) Private (customer-hosted control plane).
00:26:20 - Carlos: For the reference arch, include network flow, port lists, and IAM trust boundaries.
00:26:40 - Maya: Yep. We'll call out ports for control plane, model pulls, metrics, and KMS endpoints.
00:27:15 - Ethan: Anything on support SLAs and escalation paths for marketplace customers?
00:27:30 - Priya: We'll need an initial support SLA listed and escalation contacts. Also need an escalation playbook for incidents that affect customers.
00:27:55 - Maya: Redwood can provide support tiers; for marketplace customers we usually suggest a standard SLA and an enterprise tier with 24/7 coverage. We'll share sample SLA doc.
00:28:30 - [00:28:45] - Anika: Testing harness — do you provide a bench tool?

00:28:55 - Maya: Yes, our bench harness is a small repo and a set of scripts for smoke/perf/regression tests. We'll share a link. Note: transcript may say "bench hash" incorrectly.
00:29:40 - Ethan: Ok let's align deadlines. We called out next steps in chat. Any other open questions?
00:29:55 - Carlos: One more — model compatibility: some customers use mixed precision and custom kernels. Will Redwood accept custom kernels?
00:30:15 - Maya: We support custom kernels as long as they adhere to our runtime ABI. For most partners standard kernels plus quantization are enough; for custom we have an onboarding process. We'll include the ABI doc.
00:31:00 - Priya: Excellent. We're tracking legal sign-off separately and will push once the EDF is ready.
00:31:25 - Maya: I'll add a note about data retention options (90/180/365) and purge flows.
00:31:45 - Anika: Great.
00:32:00 - [00:32:20] - Ethan: Recap: Maya shares reference arch + manifest template, Ethan sends marketplace checklist, Aurora provides staging creds and sample workloads. We'll aim to have staging ready by 2026-10-14 and a go/no-go on 2026-10-21.
00:32:50 - Carlos: Sounds good.
00:33:10 - [00:33:40] - Priya: Any competitive intel we should be aware of? CloudMart has a faster onboarding for VM images but less flexibility on private control planes. NovaEdge pushes a fully managed expensive variant. We'll call out differentiation in listing.
00:34:05 - Maya: Noted. We'll highlight our unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private and cost controls like batching/quant profiles.
00:34:40 - Ethan: Ok folks, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
00:35:00 - Carlos: Thanks.
00:35:10 - [End of recorded transcript excerpt — remaining time was Q&A and scheduling items, minor crosstalk and a couple of dropped words in the auto-transcript.]

Recap / Next Steps: See action items. Attachments to be shared: reference_arch_v1.pdf (diagram), marketplace_checklist.xlsx, bench-harness link, SOC2 redacted, sample manifest.json.

Notes about transcript quality: medium — a few proper nouns mangled (AuroraCloud sometimes as Aurora Cloud, KV cache as "kitty cache" on auto-transcribe).
